atascado.accionArea: Review with the teams which shared dependency is holding blocked tasks
atascado.comun: When it repeats, something everyone waits for is usually missing: a review, an environment or a person from another team.
atascado.senal: There are tasks in progress that already exceed the lead time in which the team finishes almost everything it starts.
causas: Dependency on another team or on someone outside
The task was bigger than expected
The team has started other things and nobody pushes it
Waiting for review or testing
preguntas: What does each of these tasks need to move forward today?
Can any of them be split and delivered in parts?
Do they depend on someone outside the team?

plan.paso: Walk the board from right to left in the daily meeting, starting with these tasks
Agree for each one who unblocks it, or ask another person in the team for help
If it is too big, split it and deliver the first part

atascado.comprobar: In two weeks no task should be above the usual range.
atascado.respaldo: Flow metrics: work item age (Daniel Vacanti).

demasiado_a_la_vez.accionArea: Limit what comes into the area until what is started gets done
demasiado_a_la_vez.comun: When it repeats, the excess usually comes from above: more work enters the area than it can finish.
demasiado_a_la_vez.senal: Work in progress has grown and tasks take longer, without more being delivered.
causas: New work starts before the previous work is done
Interruptions and changes of priority
Long waits that invite picking up another task
preguntas: How many tasks can the team carry at once without them stalling?
Why was new work started: was it more urgent or was the other work blocked?

plan.paso: Agree a work in progress limit; to start, the number of people in the team
While at the limit, start nothing new: help finish first
Review the limit every two weeks with this data

demasiado_a_la_vez.comprobar: In four weeks work in progress should fall and lead time should return to its usual range.
demasiado_a_la_vez.respaldo: Little's law and the Kanban method.

sprint_no_cumple.accionArea: Review how sprint commitments are set in the area
sprint_no_cumple.comun: When it repeats, look at how the area plans: commitments set from outside or shared interruptions.
sprint_no_cumple.senal: A significant part of the work is carried over to the next sprint, sprint after sprint.
causas: More is committed than the team really delivers
Stories that are too big
Unplanned work that comes in mid-sprint
preguntas: How much do we deliver on average in recent sprints and how much do we commit to?
What do the carried over tasks have in common?

plan.paso: Commit based on the average delivered in the last three sprints
Reserve part of the capacity for unplanned work
Split the stories that do not fit in half a sprint

sprint_no_cumple.comprobar: In three sprints carried over work should fall below 30%.
sprint_no_cumple.respaldo: Scrum Guide; planning with real deliveries.

pendiente_crece.accionArea: Agree with the business what comes in and what is archived from the backlog
pendiente_crece.comun: When it repeats, the area receives more than it can do. It is a conversation about priorities with the business, not with the teams.
pendiente_crece.senal: More work comes in than goes out, week after week.
causas: Everything requested comes in, with no filter
The team's capacity has dropped
There is old work that no longer makes sense and nobody closes
preguntas: What part of the backlog would we really do in the next three months?
Who decides what comes in and with what criteria?

plan.paso: Review the backlog with the product owner and archive what has not moved for months
Agree what information and what value a request needs to come in
If more keeps coming in than goes out, decide with the business what will not be done

pendiente_crece.comprobar: In four weeks what goes out should match what comes in.

mucha_espera.accionArea: Find the shared step where tasks wait and give it capacity
mucha_espera.comun: When it repeats, it is usually in a step the teams share: review, testing, deployment or approval.
mucha_espera.senal: Tasks spend more time waiting than in active work.
causas: Reviews or tests that pile up
Dependencies on other teams
Blocks that nobody resolves
preguntas: In which status does work stop most, and why?
Who can review or test, and when do they do it?

plan.paso: Agree an internal deadline to attend to the status where work waits most
Give priority to reviewing and testing over starting new work
If the wait is on another team, take the dependency up with its team lead

mucha_espera.comprobar: In four weeks waiting should fall below half of lead time.

retrabajo.accionArea: Review how requirements arrive and what counts as done
retrabajo.comun: When it repeats, review what is shared: how requirements arrive and what counts as done.
retrabajo.senal: Many tasks go back to a status they had already been through.
causas: Unclear acceptance criteria
Late reviews that find big problems
A definition of done that is not met
preguntas: Why did the latest tasks go back?
Are the acceptance criteria clear before starting?

plan.paso: Review the last five tasks that went back and note the reason
Strengthen the definition of done and the acceptance criteria
Show the work halfway, not only at the end

retrabajo.comprobar: In four weeks rework should fall below 20%.

errores_capacidad.accionArea: Reserve fixed capacity for quality and automated tests
errores_capacidad.comun: When it repeats, look at the shared base: a platform, a test environment or the lack of automated tests.
errores_capacidad.senal: A large and growing part of done work is bugs.
causas: Accumulated technical debt
Few automated tests
The symptom is fixed, not the cause
preguntas: Which bugs repeat, and in which part of the system?
How much capacity do we want to dedicate to quality on a stable basis?

plan.paso: Group the bugs of the last month by cause and by part of the system
Reserve a fixed part of each sprint to tackle those causes
Add automated tests in the areas with most bugs

errores_capacidad.comprobar: In eight weeks bugs should fall below 30% of done work.

todo_al_final.accionArea: Ask for smaller stories and validate during the sprint, not at the end
todo_al_final.comun: When it repeats, it is usually a habit of the area: big stories or validation that only arrives at the end.
todo_al_final.titulo: Everything lands at the end of the sprint
todo_al_final.senal: Most tasks are closed in the last two days of the sprint.
causas: Big stories that only finish at the end
Review and testing concentrated at the end
Closed in bulk for the sprint review
preguntas: What prevents finishing tasks mid-sprint?
Is it closed in Jira when done, or before the review?

plan.paso: Split the stories so they can be finished in a few days
Review and test every day, not at the end
Close in Jira the moment something is done

todo_al_final.comprobar: In three sprints less than half should be closed in the last two days.

entregas_irregulares.accionArea: Identify the dependencies or windows that set the delivery rhythm
entregas_irregulares.comun: When it repeats, look for shared dependencies or deployment windows that set the rhythm for everyone.
entregas_irregulares.senal: What gets delivered changes a lot from one week to the next.
causas: Tasks of very different sizes
Dependencies that arrive in bursts
Bulk closures
preguntas: Do the weak weeks coincide with something: holidays, incidents, dependencies?
How big are the tasks that take longest?

plan.paso: Review the lowest weeks and note the cause
Even out task sizes when refining them
Reduce external dependencies in what gets committed

entregas_irregulares.comprobar: In eight weeks the weekly variation should fall.

estimaciones_no_predicen.accionArea: Simplify estimation: count tasks instead of points
estimaciones_no_predicen.comun: When it repeats, the problem is the estimation method, not the teams. Counting tasks is usually enough.
estimaciones_no_predicen.senal: Tasks with few points take as long as or longer than tasks with many points.
causas: The estimate measures something other than duration
Waiting weighs more than real work
Estimated in a hurry or without knowing the task well
preguntas: What do we use points for today?
Would counting tasks serve us better than adding up points?

plan.paso: Compare in a retro several small tasks that took a long time
If tasks are of similar size, plan by counting tasks instead of points
If points are kept, estimate after refining and not before

estimaciones_no_predicen.comprobar: In twelve weeks the relation between points and duration should improve, or points should stop being used for planning.

todo_urgente.accionArea: Agree with the business what is urgent and limit its volume
todo_urgente.comun: When it repeats, priority is decided outside the teams. Agree with the business what is really urgent.
todo_urgente.senal: A very large part of the work comes in with the highest priority.
causas: There is no shared criterion for what is urgent
Marking as urgent is the only way to get something attended to
Several people make requests without coordinating
preguntas: What would happen if these tasks waited a week?
Who decides the priority and with what criteria?

plan.paso: Define with the business what is urgent, with two or three examples
Create an urgent lane with a limit, for example one task at a time
Review every month what came in as urgent and whether it was

todo_urgente.comprobar: In eight weeks what is marked as urgent should fall below 25%.

urgente_no_rapido.accionArea: Use priority to really order the work
urgente_no_rapido.comun: When it repeats, priority is not used to order the work in the area.
urgente_no_rapido.senal: Tasks with the highest priority take as long as the rest.
causas: Priority is not used to order the work
There are so many urgent tasks that they cancel each other out
Urgent work waits in the same queues as everything else
preguntas: Does the team look at priority when choosing the next task?
How many urgent tasks are there at once?

plan.paso: Order the backlog by priority and respect that order when choosing
Create an urgent lane that skips the review queues
If almost everything is urgent, deal first with the case "Everything is urgent"

urgente_no_rapido.comprobar: In eight weeks urgent work should clearly take less time than the rest.

datos_poco_fiables.accionArea: Agree how Jira is used before drawing conclusions
datos_poco_fiables.comun: When it repeats, there is no shared agreement on how Jira is used: statuses, closures and sprints.
datos_poco_fiables.senal: Jira does not fully reflect how the team works, and that affects the measures.
causas: Tasks are moved in Jira after the work is done
The status flow is not used as designed
Fields that are not filled in
preguntas: Do we move tasks in Jira when they really change status?
Which fields do we always need to fill in?

plan.paso: Agree three rules of use: move when starting, move when finishing and fill in the points
Review the status flow so it reflects the real work
plan.quien: Team lead with the Jira admin

plan.paso: Repeat the data check in four weeks

datos_poco_fiables.comprobar: In four weeks the data quality warnings should disappear or fall.

no_planificado.accionArea: Create a single entry point for unplanned work
no_planificado.comun: When it repeats, it usually comes from the same source: support, incidents or direct requests to the area.
no_planificado.senal: A significant part of done work came in after the sprint had started.
causas: Production incidents
Direct requests that skip planning
preguntas: Where does unplanned work come in?

plan.paso: Reserve fixed capacity for unplanned work
Create a single entry point for urgent work

no_planificado.comprobar: What comes in mid-sprint should fall below 15%.

grupo_plazo.accionArea: Review with the slower group where work stops: reviews, environments or dependencies
grupo_plazo.comun: When a group takes longer on the same task type and size, there is usually a step that waits more: review, testing, access or answers from another team.
grupo_plazo.titulo: A group takes longer on the same type of work
grupo_plazo.senal: Within the same task type and size, a group takes clearly longer than the rest.
causas: Longer waits in review or testing
Dependencies on other teams or on the client
Less access to environments, data or people who decide
Tasks that arrive less well defined
preguntas: In which status does this group's work stop most?
Does it have the same access to environments, reviews and decisions as the rest?
Do its tasks arrive as well defined?

plan.paso: Compare with the group the time in each status and pick the step that waits most
Agree a deadline for that step and who attends to it
plan.quien: Team leads of the teams involved

plan.paso: Review the difference in the next monthly comparison

grupo_plazo.comprobar: In two months the difference in lead time should fall below 25%.
grupo_plazo.respaldo: Stratified comparison by task type and size; flow metrics.

grupo_calidad.accionArea: Review with the group how requirements arrive and what counts as done
grupo_calidad.comun: When a group goes back or reopens more on the same type of work, the agreement on what is done or how it is validated usually fails.
grupo_calidad.titulo: A group goes back or reopens more
grupo_calidad.senal: Within the same task type and size, a group has clearly more rework or more reopened tasks.
causas: Unclear acceptance criteria for that group
Late validation, or validation by another team
A definition of done different from the rest
Fewer automated tests
preguntas: Does this group use the same definition of done as the rest?
Who validates its work, and when?
Why were the latest tasks reopened?

plan.paso: Review with the group the last ten tasks that went back and note the reason
Align the definition of done and the acceptance criteria with the rest
Validate during the work, not only at the end

grupo_calidad.comprobar: In two months the group's rework and reopened tasks should get closer to the rest.
grupo_calidad.respaldo: Stratified comparison by task type and size; definition of done (Scrum Guide).

grupo_agent_ready.accionArea: Agree with the group a ticket template with acceptance criteria and references
grupo_agent_ready.comun: When a group writes less complete tickets, a shared template or refinement time is usually missing.
grupo_agent_ready.titulo: A group has its backlog less ready for AI agents
grupo_agent_ready.senal: The share of tickets ready for an AI agent is clearly lower in one group than in the rest.
causas: There is no ticket template, or it is not used
Refinement happens verbally and is not written down
Acceptance criteria are agreed outside the tool
preguntas: Which ticket template does this group use?
Where are the acceptance criteria written down?

plan.paso: Review with the group five recent tickets against the agent readiness rubric
Adopt a template with description, acceptance criteria and references
Repeat the measure in a month

grupo_agent_ready.comprobar: In a month the group's share of ready tickets should get closer to the rest.

backlog_no_listo.accionArea: Agree a shared ticket template in the area
backlog_no_listo.comun: When it repeats in several teams, there is no shared agreement on how a ticket is written.
backlog_no_listo.titulo: The backlog is not ready for AI agents
backlog_no_listo.senal: Less than half of new tickets meet four of the five criteria of the rubric.
causas: Short descriptions, or descriptions that repeat the title
No written acceptance criteria
Tickets that are too big or have open dependencies
preguntas: Which criterion fails most in the team's tickets?
Could someone outside the team do this ticket without asking?

plan.paso: Look at which criterion of the rubric fails most and start with that one
Add to the ticket template a section for acceptance criteria and another for references
Split tickets of more than five points before starting them

backlog_no_listo.comprobar: In a month more than half of new tickets should be ready for an AI agent.
